subject: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@deepscale.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan

Hi Rajiv —

Thanks again for the candid convo yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a focused proposal to move DeepScale from your current 8-GPU reserved pool to a 16-GPU reserved pool as part of the upcoming contract renewal. High-level bullets below and the attached term sheet for numbers: redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf.

Summary highlights:
- Upgrade: Reserved pool increases from 8 GPUs → 16 GPUs (single region, us-west-2).
- Monthly commit: revised to 2.4 million token-equivalent units / month (details in proforma).
- Throughput guarantee: 99th percentile per-request latency cap of 180ms for standard gen workloads up to 2k context, with a burst path allowing 1.5x throughput for short windows.
- Pricing: blended per-token rate for committed usage, with overage band at a discounted rate; see spreadsheet billing_proforma_2028Q3.xlsx.
- Activation plan: staged cutover over 4 weeks — week 0 (capacity reservation + billing amendment), week 1 (canary routing at 10%), week 2 (50% traffic), week 3 (100% primary).
- Ops runbook: draft cutover_runbook_draft.md attached — includes rollback criteria, KV-cache warmup, and canary metrics.

Ask: Please confirm if the proposed monthly commit and the staged activation timeline look reasonable. Once you sign the term sheet we’ll kick off the capacity reservation and schedule the cutover window with your SRE team. I’ve CC’d Aditya for the runtime/compatibility notes and Marissa for contracting/billing.

Attachments:
- redwood_term_sheet_v3.pdf (PDF, 212KB)
- cutover_runbook_draft.md (text, 18KB)
- billing_proforma_2028Q3.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@deepscale.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Cc: DeepScale Ops <ops@deepscale.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan

Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the doc set. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you confirm the billing start date for the upgraded commit? We need alignment with our fiscal quarter cutover (targeting 2028-09-01).
2) We run a custom model ensemble that stores large KV caches; will the KV warmup described in the runbook be sufficient to avoid cold penalties during week 1 canary? Ops is worried about transient 5–10% latency spikes for the first 10M tokens.
3) Is there any short-term credit we can apply given the timing overlap of our existing commit and the new commit (to avoid double-paying during the cutover week)?

If you can answer those 3, I’ll take the term sheet to procurement and loop back.

—Rajiv
CTO, DeepScale

On Fri, 03 Aug 2028 at 12:05 PM PDT, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Rajiv — thanks, we can accommodate those asks. Details below.
>
> 1) Billing: we can set the ASP (activation start period) to 2028-09-01 and pro-rate the first invoice for days in September. We’ll include a one-week overlap buffer credit so you are not double-charged for both pools during the canary window — see billing_proforma_2028Q3.xlsx tab 'CutoverCredits'.
>
> 2) KV warmup and latency: Aditya and Engineering recommend a two-stage warmup: pre-warm on reserved instances with a synthetic prefix population 48 hours before canary, then a progressive cache population during the 10% canary window. We’ll instrument a rolling monitor and set automatic rollback if 95th/99th latency exceeds the agreed thresholds or token error rates increase. Aditya — can you add the memory/eviction configs we should apply?
>
> 3) Credits: commercial is willing to put a small one-off credit to offset overlap risk (ref Appendix A in the term sheet). Final amount will be reflected in DocuSign.
>
> I’ll tentatively schedule the cutover beginning week of 2028-09-04; if ops needs a different week we can shift.
>
> Best,
> Irene
>
> —

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>, Rajiv Shah <rajiv@deepscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 06 Aug 2028 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan

Hey team —

Technical confirmations and a few operational notes:

- Warmup plan: we’ll run a background prefix population job that writes artificial keys sized similarly to your production KV objects. Runbook already includes the script and the required GPU reservation window. Pre-warm window: 48–72 hours.
- Memory config: set the KV cache high-water mark to 85% and evict oldest-first with a 2-second grace TTL for new keys during the canary. This reduces churn and gives the model steady-state hit rates.
- Canary thresholds: automatic rollback if 99th latency > 300ms for more than 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets OR error rate > 0.8%.
- Autoscaling soak: for the first 14 days after full cutover, we’ll allow controlled autoscaling spikes to handle steady ramp; these spikes are outside the committed capacity but billed as temporary burst usage at the agreed overage discount.

A note on throughput guarantees: the 180ms 99th we quoted assumes your requested context lengths. If you push longer sequences (>3k context) we should re-profile the model and may need to adjust the SLA.

I’ll coordinate a brief runbook walk-through with DeepScale Ops next week.

- Aditya
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@deepscale.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 10:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan

Rajiv —

Thanks for the questions. Commercial confirmations:

- Billing start date: set to 2028-09-01 as requested. First invoice is pro-rated; we’ll show the one-week overlap credit as a separate line item.
- Credit amount: pending a short internal approval but we’re targeting a one-off credit equal to 25% of the pro-rated cost of the overlapped week. This will be captured in the DocuSign addendum.
- DocuSign: I’ve uploaded the final term sheet with the credit placeholder and routing for signatures. You should receive a DocuSign link in the next hour: https://docusign.com/link/abcd-1234-renewal.

Next steps: once the signed DocuSign is returned we’ll provision the reservation, schedule the SRE runbook session, and confirm cutover dates. If procurement needs an updated PO/Order Form we’ll generate one within 24 hours of signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewals Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@deepscale.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 09 Aug 2028 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Capacity rebalance & 8→16 reserved pool — term sheet and cutover plan

Appreciate the fast follow. The billing start date and overlap credit look good; ops and procurement both signed off internally. I’ve forwarded the DocuSign to procurement and they’ll route it back signed by EOD Monday.

One ask from ops: can we add a 24-hour rollback guard after reaching 100% traffic so we have a clean fallback window if we see production anomalies? If that’s okay we’ll sign sooner.

Thanks — excited to get this live.

—Rajiv
